textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a human HEPATOCYTE (liver cell) shown IN CONTEXT, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around each structure so labels can be attached later. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark charcoal background with NO border, NO frame, NO vignette and NO letterbox bars. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette of soft dusty tints (never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, and each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. COMPOSITION: one large central hepatocyte drawn as a chunky POLYHEDRAL block cell with flat straight faces and blunt angled corners (like a rounded-off many-sided brick), roughly as tall as it is wide - NOT a smooth sphere, NOT a tall column. It is wedged between two partially-shown neighbouring hepatocytes, one at the right edge and one at the bottom-left, drawn simpler and slightly faded so the central cell dominates. TWO DIFFERENT FACES, the whole point of the picture: (1) along the LEFT side of the central cell runs a wide dusky-red BLOOD CHANNEL (hepatic sinusoid) lined by a thin, perforated endothelial sheet with small round holes; between that lining and the cell's left face is a narrow pale fluid gap (space of Disse) into which the cell's left surface projects a fringe of short, irregular, finger-like MICROVILLI of uneven length; (2) along the RIGHT side, where the central cell presses against its neighbour, the two membranes leave a tiny golden-green GROOVE between them - the bile canaliculus - a small channel belonging to BOTH cells, with a few short microvilli poking into it and a short dark thickening at each of its two shoulders marking the sealing tight junctions. The cell's remaining faces touch neighbours flatly. INTERIOR, revealed by a neat quarter cut-away: TWO large round nuclei side by side (binucleation is characteristic of hepatocytes and must be shown), each pale blue-violet with a speckled chromatin texture and one distinctly darker round nucleolus inside; a dense supply of small warm-ochre oval MITOCHONDRIA with faint internal cristae lines scattered all through the cytoplasm; folded stacks of dusty-rose ROUGH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM sheets studded with tiny ribosome dots, gathered near the nuclei; a pale sage-green branching tubular network of SMOOTH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM filling a broad zone of the cytoplasm; a few small round teal PEROXISOMES with a slightly denser core; a few muted-plum LYSOSOMES; a curved turquoise stack of GOLGI cisternae near the bile groove; clusters of tiny dusty-yellow GLYCOGEN GRANULES arranged in little rosette clumps; and two or three smooth pale cream-yellow round LIPID DROPLETS. Do NOT draw a bacterial cell wall, nucleoid, plasmids or flagellum; do NOT draw cilia or a dense regular brush border anywhere (hepatocyte microvilli are short, sparse and irregular); do NOT draw one large central vacuole or chloroplasts; do NOT draw the bile canaliculus as a tube running through the middle of the cytoplasm - it is a groove BETWEEN two cells; do NOT put the blood channel and the bile groove on the same face. CRITICAL GEOMETRY CORRECTIONS - obey these exactly. (a) THE BLOOD CHANNEL: the hepatic sinusoid is an OPEN LANE of blood running VERTICALLY down the LEFT side of the picture and continuing off both the TOP and the BOTTOM edge of the frame, like a river seen from the side. It is a wide open channel with a thin perforated lining sheet on each bank, NOT a round blob, NOT a ball, NOT another cell, and it must NOT be joined to the hepatocyte by a narrow neck, stalk, bridge or tube. (b) THE BILE CANALICULUS: it is a TINY NARROW SLOT, no wider than a hair, formed where the FLAT RIGHT FACE of the central cell lies directly against the FLAT LEFT FACE of its neighbour and each membrane has a shallow half-round notch, so the two notches together make a small gutter running vertically along the join. Draw it as a thin vertical channel in the seam between two touching flat walls. It is absolutely NOT a barrel, NOT a spool, NOT a bowtie, NOT a tube or bridge or tunnel connecting the two cells, and NOT a hole inside the cytoplasm. (c) THE TWO NUCLEI: they must NOT sit symmetrically side by side at the same height like a pair of eyes. Stagger them - one larger nucleus set high and slightly left, the second smaller one set lower and to the right, partly overlapping in depth. (d) THE NEIGHBOURING CELLS: only partial slices of them, cropped by the frame edge, drawn plainer and dimmer, and NOT identical mirror copies of the central cell. (e) THE SMOOTH ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM is an irregular interwoven mesh of looping tubules, NOT a tree, NOT a branching coral, NOT a plant or fern shape.  FURTHER CORRECTIONS: the neighbouring hepatocyte at the RIGHT edge must be visibly DIFFERENT from the central cell - show only a NARROW VERTICAL STRIP of it, containing just one nucleus and a sparse scatter of organelles, and never a mirrored duplicate of the central cell's interior. The bile canaliculus between them must be a THIN DARK SLOT no thicker than a pencil line, a simple narrow vertical gap in the seam between the two flat walls - never a barrel, capsule, spool, cylinder or lozenge shape. Leave a clear band of empty dark background along the top and the bottom of the picture so that labels can be placed there. FINAL COMPOSITION RULE: the picture must NOT be mirror-symmetric. Place the central hepatocyte slightly LEFT of centre and let ONLY A NARROW VERTICAL SLICE of one neighbouring hepatocyte appear along the right edge, cut off by the frame; that slice shows just a plain cytoplasm with one nucleus and a couple of mitochondria, and its contents must NOT mirror the central cell's. Do NOT draw any thin dark line, wire or tether running from the bile canaliculus into the cytoplasm. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere in the image.
